primitives.name: Task Persistence Regime Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Known Weaknesses - Task persistence uses existing `CockpitTask` payload storage when DB exists and in-memory fallback in stub mode; deeper first-class Prisma fields can be reviewed later.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M': 'mode indicator {0,1} for DB vs in-memory', 'T': 'task identifier'}
primitives.assumptions: Payload storage is binary and deterministic based on environment state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In stub mode, task integrity is not guaranteed due to ephemeral memory.

layer2.mapping: The mode selection function M(T) mirrors a Boolean switch in GSI's probabilistic task graph, where each task T maps to a persistence kernel K(T) ∈ {DB, MEM}.
layer2.telemetry: Observable via task completion logs and memory footprint metrics.

primitives.name: Worker Activation State Indicator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - BullMQ facade is safe/manual when Redis is absent; no real worker process was started.
primitives.assumptions: Worker process lifecycle depends directly on Redis presence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R=0, W remains inactive regardless of task queue content.

layer2.mapping: Activation kernel W(R) = 1 iff R=1; otherwise W=0. This defines a control-theoretic feedback loop in GSE’s task orchestration layer.
layer2.telemetry: Process start time and resource allocation flags.

primitives.name: UI Rendering Status Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Jarvis runtime is library-wired, not yet rendered into the cockpit UI.
primitives.assumptions: Runtime integration is decoupled from UI rendering pipeline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: U=0 implies J≠0 but no visual output.

layer2.mapping: Rendering kernel U(J) = 1 iff J is fully initialized and bound to cockpit context. Otherwise U=0.
layer2.telemetry: DOM element existence and event listener registration.
